summary: The study investigates the electrical properties of high permittivity thin film nanolaminates composed of Ta2O5–HfO2, Ta2O5–ZrO2, and ZrO2–HfO2 deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The films were grown on silicon substrates with a silicon nitride passivation layer. The dielectric constants of the nanolaminates ranged from 12 to 14, and leakage current densities were in the range of 10^-8 to 10^-7 A/cm2 at 1 MV/cm. The study also examined the effect of postdeposition annealing and the impact of film thickness on dielectric properties.
evidence: Thin (~10 nm) films comprising of Ta2O5–HfO2, Ta2O5–ZrO2, and ZrO2–HfO2 nanolaminates were deposited and characterized for possible gate dielectric applications. These films were deposited on silicon substrates using atomic layer deposition. The dielectric constants of these films were in 12–14 range and the leakage currents in 2.6×10^-8–4.2×10^-7 A/cm2 range at 1 MV/cm electric field.
